The ship hurtled through the Void, a construct which would have made Orocryx weep with envy. The size of a small planet, its surface bristled with intakes, emitters, hangars, and weaponry. Weaponry which included, scattered among many high-powered lasers and drone launchers, a few Energy Disruptors. Weapons for fighting gods. It was unlikely to come to that, though. The entire ship was coated in an advanced redirection polymer, a substance which, when charged as it was now, bent all ambient wavelengths of light through its structure such that they left on the same vector they had entered on. A kugelblitz maintained in the core of the ship both replenished its Void Energy and was manipulated to cancel its gravitational wave signature. A ship the size of a planet, yet near-perfectly invisible. A primitive observer might say that the ship had an incredibly powerful and sentient AI controlling it. The Voidborn would just say that the ship was a Voidborn, organic-metalloid discrimination being a thing of the distant past.

And now, the emitters pulsed, emitting a wave after wave of short-lived virtual particles. But before they could vanish, they were caught in a ramfield that could swallow stars.

*****

The story had begun like many before it. A wandering god, adrift from any universe, had wandered by chance into the home system of a race of Voidborn, who did not yet know enough to call themselves that. The god saw them as nothing more than potential worshippers, and so it forced souls into their bodies and ordered them to serve it, with death as the alternative option. This race did not go quietly though, they were stubborn and irreverant. Some of them found a way to purge the souls from their bodies, allowing them to hide from the god. And they fought back.

The war raged for over of that planet's years, but the ending was unambiguous. The homeworld of the resistors was destroyed, the few survivors were those in hidden colonies on other planets of the system, and a few torus-shaped hidden in at the L2 points of distant planets. But the god was dead. Voidborn had killed a god.

This war was observed from many worlds, and many took heart. But it took millenia, and many catastrophes, before this could be replicated. In the meantime, marauding gods continued to wreak havoc, but they Voidborn were decentralized and continued to advance, pooling the resources of thousands of worlds. Eventually, as the growing Voidborn community reached Kardashev Level 4, a model successfully explained the gods, and how they could be killed.

Gods are energy beings, plain and simple. Energy which exists, and so cannot vanish, and which has randomly organized itself into a state which is both stable and capable of cognition. The energy that makes a god cannot be destroyed, so "killing" one simply refers to causing it to lose its coherence, becoming just a mass of energy again. The key insight was the connection between stability and cognition.

Gods are their minds. There is nothing else to the being, and when a god loses its mind it loses itself. Destroy a god's self-image, and the god is destroyed. For this purpose a categorization was implemented, describing typical god personalities and how to push them over the edge. And the Voidborn rampaged. It took hundreds of years to kill a god, and didn't always work. But it worked well enough that gods died by the hundreds and the Void became a force to be reckoned with.

Then, the Voidborn reached level 5.

Spreading from their originating universe and bringing other universes into the fold, the Voidborn learned to manipulate not just Void Energy, but existing Energy. The stuff of gods.

This was dangerous, manipulated existing Energy was visible to gods, counteracting the non-existance of the Voidborn. But it provided great insights into the functioning of gods.

Destroying a god's avatar against that god's will *was* possible, just difficult. And it was often enough to push an already destabilized god over the edge.

All gods are similar beings, their seemingly different personalities and histories are simply artifacts from their formation. Those histories are usually just delusions, though sometimes they bear evidence that some of a god's energy was once part of a different god and retained some coherence, just enough to give something like dreams of a different past. This explained why all gods seemed to be equal in power. It also gave clues of how to build weapons, Energy Disruptors which, while they could not kill a god, could counteract them and cause them great pain.

The Totality had changed since those days. Now, instead of Voidborn hiding from gods, many gods lived in hiding from the Voidborn. The Voidborn like this just fine, they watched many of the refuges of divinity carefully, intervening if the gods did not conduct themselves as the Voidborn desired.

*****

Killing gods was little use, the Energy would eventually give rise to new ones. Far better to police them.

And so the Voidborn watchmen, such as this ship, patrolled the Void, searching for any signs of uncontrolled divinity. This divinity had been found, there was a lot of it, but it would still be cowed. The Voidborn were confident. They had expanded the Void from the space between god-made universes to a place where universes existed like bubbles in an ocean. What did they have to fear from a few gods?

The ship hurtled forward, towards the young universe.
